text:
Maya: Console team flagged a weird p99 for /v1/generate in eu-west over the last 20m. Rollup p99 = 1.2s but when I split by model_variant none exceed 800ms. sample_count is tiny (~90). Anyone seen a mismatch like this?
Noah: saw that too. Could be t-digest merge artifact across different origin tags (variant vs untagged).
Jules: Can you paste the rollup vs split numbers? Need to decide if it's telemetry noise or real.
Maya: Rollup (route=/v1/generate, 20m): p50 150ms p95 380ms p99 1200ms sample_count 92.
Split by model_variant: variant-x p99 210ms count 50, variant-y p99 720ms count 40. No room for 1.2s unless other samples exist.
infra-bot: Deploy record: route-attribute-change at 1735220000 made field "model_variant" optional in some routers.
Noah: Bingo. Some requests lost the variant tag and ended up in an "untagged" bucket; when we merge t-digests across tagged+untagged with tiny high-latency outliers, the rollup p99 can spike above any individual bucket p99.
Maya: Product is worried. They want to avoid showing impossible numbers to customers. Ideas?
Jules: Short-term: add an explicit provenance badge on rollup percentiles when we detect mixed-origin data, e.g. "mixed labels" with tooltip. Also surface sample origins on hover.
Noah: Backend change: when computing rollups, include origin_counts summary. But careful about response bloat for wide-rollups. We can return only top-3 origins and an "others" count.
Maya: UX preference: show badge by default in console, but keep API cheap by default. Console queries can pass ?provenance=1.
Jules: Server should also set a "mixed_origin" flag when origins in merged set are incompatible (e.g., some have variant, some don't). If mixed_origin=true, the p99 should be annotated: "computed across mixed origin labels" instead of silently wrong.
Noah: Implementation plan: aggregator will maintain per-origin t-digests for frequent origins. For low-cardinality queries we can compute full breakdown; for high-cardinality, compute counts and approximate quantiles for top origins only.
Maya: Can we add a light mitigation first: if rollup p99 > max(per-origin p99) + 50ms and untagged_count > 0, show callout "possible mixed-origin artifact" with link to raw sample explorer. That avoids heavy compute initially.
telemetry-bot: Note: created perf ticket #T-4620 "rollup mixed-origin detection + provenance API" assigned to Noah.
Noah: I'll prototype the API change: respond with fields p50,p95,p99,sample_count and if provenance requested, include top_origins as a serialized string list like "variant-x:50:p99=210" to keep JSON flat.
Jules: Good call on serialized strings to avoid nested objects in responses. Server should also log when mixed_origin persists > 5m to trigger infra alert.
Maya: Timeline?
Noah: PR with prototype in 48h, console badge in 72h. We'll gate heavy per-origin quantiles behind a feature flag.
Jules: Product approved. Also we should retroactively scan last 24h for other deploys that toggled optional attributes; there may be similar artifacts.
Maya: Thanks all. Once PR is up tag me and I'll coordinate a small note for customers explaining "visualization artifact" if needed.
Noah: Adding link to this thread in the PR.
infra-bot: Search hint: look for deploys touching router attrs between 1735218000-1735222000.
Maya: Endnote: long-term, we should define a rollup contract that percentiles are only shown when merging compatible provenance or else require explicit aggregation semantics.
Jules: Agreed. We'll draft a spec after the prototype.
